'''''Serapias lingua''''', commonly known as '''tongue-orchid'''<ref name=BSBI07>{{BSBI 2007 |accessdate=2014-10-17 }}</ref> or the '''tongue ''Serapias''''', is a species of [[orchid]] native to the [[Mediterranean]].<ref name=eb/>

==Habitat and distribution==
''Serapias lingua'' can be found in damp meadows, open fields, marshlands, and sometimes [[garrigue]] of Portugal, Spain, Malta, France, Italy, Yugoslavia, Albania, Greece, the Mediterranean islands west of Crete, and western North Africa.{{Citation needed|date=March 2013}} It has also been recorded from some sites in southern England, where it is unclear if it is naturally occurring.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://bsbi.org/taxa/2cd4p9h.3hx4dr/serapias-lingua?q=serapias%20lingua|title=Serapias lingua|website=BSBI}}</ref>

==Flowering==
''Serapias lingua'' flowers from April to May or early June. The plant grows from 10 to 30 cm, with 2–8 flowers per spike. The [[Labellum (botany)|labellum]] can be yellowish, pink, or magenta.<ref>{{Cite book|title=Wild Orchids of Britain and Europe|last=Davies|first=Paul|year=1983|isbn=0-7011-2642-6}}</ref>
